coverage.assessment: Two setups were thinned. The world's applause no longer precedes 'History broke in halves'. The magnet's mysterious radiation no longer grounds the radium comparison or 'another radiating matter'.
Hay, King, Pauncefote, Cassini and Walcott are clearly placed. King's spring stop in Washington and the return date of January 30, 1901 are intact. 'All his predecessors' resolves to Hay.

Hay's speech is attributed to him ('laughed Hay') and repeated in p7. The condensation, marked by a visible ellipsis, is plan-authorized, though it drops the 'being sick a good part of the time' beat.

Facts are accurate and Walcott moves Pteraspis. The historian's disclaimer of any concern with scientific correctness, and the hedges 'even in secret' and 'honest-meaning', were cut in the first draft. This is a tradeoff.
King's death is not narrated; 'dropped' and the closing 'to the end' stay prospective. 'Hay was going to wreck on it' remains forward-looking.
The litotes on lost sunshine, the 'admission' echo, the peach-blossom 'larger synthesis' joke and some opening ironies are lost. The aphoristic closers and stage-image grief are kept.
The pivot from helplessness to complexity, and geology's persistence of refuted formulas (Suess), are weakened. Unity against multiplicity remains legible overall.
All six dependencies are intact at both the local endpoint and the partner's revised text.

strengths: Adams's mistaken assumption and laughter at Hay are kept before the rescue, preserving the retrospective self-irony.
King's farewell retains the full stage-role passage ('Non doles, Paete!') and the log-cabin payoff, with King's death kept off-page.
The list of natural selection's contradictions and 'Darwinism seemed to survive only in England' preserve the double-hyphen accumulating rhythm.
The Adam/God/Satan figure and 'Hay was going to wreck on it, like King and Adams' remain prospective and verbatim.
summary: The revision preserves the chapter's main arc: relative values, Hay's China stroke, strain, the Senate, King's farewell, the magnet, unity and complexity, the Lyell rereading, Pteraspis, geology and the shark close. All eight verbatim passages and every continuity check survive. There is no must-fix defect. The new cuts, often on top of first-draft cuts, mostly remove logical hinges and verbal echoes: the setup for 'History broke in halves', the magnet's radiation premise, the 'not helplessness but complexity' pivot, the Suess persistence paradox, and 'The admission cost nothing.' Each loss is small, but together they flatten the argument and Adams's ironic voice.
